feature: Regular stock request / Backorder: Already Ordered
authorizedBy: User explicitly requested SCM Already Ordered status, mandatory PO number, optional PO ref number, and immediate line completion without SO/PO linking or further steps.
contract: Only SCM can save Already Ordered on an active Regular Backorder line.
PO number is a trimmed nonempty string of at most 120 characters; optional PO ref number is a trimmed string of at most 200 characters. Control characters and nonstrings are rejected.
Saved references are plain references; no existing synced order, vendor lookup, ETA, Sales acceptance, PO planning, or remote mutation is required.
The selected line completes atomically with a revision increment and audit event. Its reference fields remain visible to Sales and SCM after refresh.
Completed lines have no edit, decision, response, readiness, SO, or PO actions. Other lines retain their normal workflow and purchase readiness excludes completed lines.
A request with only Already Ordered and declined/closed lines is Completed if at least one is Already Ordered. Only declined/closed lines still close the request.
Detail, SQL stage view, pending/completed queues, and alerts agree. Completed lines do not demand customer replies or readiness reminders.
Foreign lines, unauthorized roles/yards, stale revisions and concurrent writes cannot corrupt or reopen completion. Special requests and other Regular types do not gain this status.
SCM UI shows both reference fields only for Already Ordered, enforces PO number, hides normal stock-check fields, explains immediate completion, and displays saved completion to both roles.
verification: Backorder and shared Special regression comparison
deployment: Scoped production overlay, additive constrained schema migration, unchanged existing records and configuration, retained rollback image, exact runtime verification.
validationClarifications: SCM uses queue=closed for completed requests; Sales uses bucket=completed. Compare unchanged lines using the same audience because SCM includes private purchase fields. These correct test inputs, without changing the completion contract.

The negative Special-route test now explicitly enables and restores the Special feature flag, checks normal-status foreign-workflow routing returns 404, and checks Already Ordered returns 400/SPECIAL_RESPONSE_STATUS_INVALID. This removes dependence on earlier suites changing the feature flag and strengthens the isolation assertion.

failureModel.partial or concurrent completion: transaction, case/line row locks, expected revision, HTTP race test
failureModel.mandatory PO bypass or hostile text: HTTP input matrix, text round-trip property, database constraints, browser escaping
failureModel.completed line reopened or false whole-r: terminal action rejection, mixed workflow, stage and readiness properties
failureModel.follow-up prompts after completion: real SCM/Sales browser with pending information and a linked PO
failureModel.migration corrupts existing data or fail: isolated migration replay and transaction rollback with unchanged row assertions
failureModel.existing shared workflow regression: captured production suite and diagnostic multiset comparison

setupActual.toolchain: Existing bounded test image; versions recorded in proofs report
setupActual.git: Preserve unrelated dirty workspace; scoped runtime overlay against captured production
setupActual.database: Disposable isolated Compose PostgreSQL; production schema migration only after verification
setupActual.knownLimit: Automatic code rollback is permitted only before any new Already Ordered rows have been saved; the additive schema and reference data are retained.
